posts.title: Christmas Films
posts.description: I'm not a huge movie buff, I don't really watch many films as I tend to lose interest half way though but over the last few years I've made a point of watching some Christmas films in the run up to the big day. There were so many I hadn't seen before and I rewatched some favourites. I decided I'd do that again this year. Mick loves watching films so he's been more than happy to watch with me. So far we've watched eleven and abandoned one but there's still four weeks until Christmas Day, plenty of time to watch a few more. The Holiday. I've seen this before but didn't think much to it. I actually enjoyed this one more the second time round and rated it 6 out of 10. Mick rated it 4 out of 10. Nativity. This had a great cast and I thought it was very funny, I'd definitely watch this again. I rated it 6 out of 10. Mick rated it 5 out of 10. Christmas with the Kranks. posts.title: Bakewell Christmas Market
posts.description: I know I said in my last post that I had shopping to do last Saturday, but in the end it was a different kind of shopping trip to the one I had planned. I was supposed to be doing shopping of the mundane sort, however, it's that time of year when the Christmas markets are beginning to be held and when I saw that Bakewell was having their Christmas market last weekend, the boring old shopping I had planned was put on hold. Bakewell is a market town in Derbyshire and it's such a lovely place to visit. The River Wye flows through the centre of town and it's a nice place to sit for a while. Although the sun was shining it was bitterly cold so we didn't linger. The market had a good selection of stalls, over a hundred in total. There were plenty of different food stalls, both things to take home for gifts and food to eat there and then. posts.title: Last Weekend
posts.description: I'm a bit late writing about our outing last weekend but I just don't know where the time's going at the moment. Well I do, I'm trying to help Eleanor out as much as I can at the moment, she's still got a few weeks to go before her due date but she looks ready to pop at any minute, and she's still working. Just over a week to go now until she takes some annual leave before her maternity leave kicks in. Anyway, back to last weekend, both Eleanor and Jacob were working on the Saturday so we had Jack for the day. It didn't rain but it was a bit damp. It didn't stop us from taking him to the park, though it did stop him from going down the slide as it was wet. He managed a good amount of time on the swings and he loved throwing the conkers we'd taken with us into the stream from the bridge above. They landed with a very satisfying splash! On Sunday we decided to pay Haworth a visit. Home to the Brontë sisters, the above photo shows the Parsonage where they lived. It was Remembrance Sunday
